text:
mari-plat: Heads-up: I'm proposing a change to billing_metrics storage — move route_id from text to bigint (we've been casting a numeric fingerprint, turns out it's stable). This will speed group-bys on billing dashboards but touches a bunch of ingest paths and console queries.

sophia: +1 for perf but big :warning: on migration complexity. What's the compatibility plan?

anil: Can we do dual columns first? `route_id_text` (existing) + `route_id_int` (new). Dual-write at ingest, fallback to text for reads until backfill completes.

mari-plat: That's the plan I sketched. Dual write + read adapter that prefers int if non-null. Backfill via windowed UPDATEs.

gabe: How big is the table? p95 rows per day? We need estimate for backfill time and IO.

mari-plat: Current retention for billing_metrics is 6 months, ~1.2B rows total (all tenants). Backfill at cluster-level will be heavy.

jess: We should avoid a global blocking backfill. Proposal: backfill per-tenant in priority order, use tenant windowing, and mark tenant as migrated when done. Add a migration_status column.

anil: Suggestion: create a new partial index on `route_id_int` for migrated tenants only to avoid index bloat while dual-write in progress.

sophia: Need to update all console queries/dashboards to prefer `route_id_int` once available. How do we avoid broken dashboards during migration?

mari-plat: We add a query layer flag `prefer_route_id_int=auto` that uses int when non-null and falls back otherwise. The console can switch to `prefer_route_id_int=true` once we verify a cohort of tenants.

gabe: What about aggregations used by billing alerts? Those run nightly on analytic workers. We must ensure they use the same read adapter.

jess: Also we need to coordinate with the cost-exec team: billing pipelines are sensitive. Any mismatch between billing and console views will trigger support tickets.

mari-plat: Agreed — rollout plan: 1) schema change (add route_id_int, migration_status) 2) dual-write in ingest (feature flag off by default) 3) backfill by tenant windows + health checks 4) switch query adapter to prefer int for canary tenants 5) monitor for 48h then flip for more tenants 6) drop text column after 90d stable.

anil: For (1) we can do `ALTER TABLE billing_metrics ADD COLUMN route_id_int bigint;` (fast) but adding indexes is heavier. Keep index creation after backfill.

sophia: Can we get an estimate for disk overhead during dual-write (no index)? Might be significant. Also VACUUM/ANALYZE schedule matters.

gabe: We should also consider a background copy approach with `pg_repack` or copy-to-new-table pattern to avoid bloat, but that adds complexity.

jess: Ops constraints — maintenance windows are limited. We should plan backfill throttles and a rate limiter.

mari-plat: Example backfill job SQL (rough):

```sql
-- backfill tenant window
UPDATE billing_metrics
SET route_id_int = (CASE WHEN route_id_text ~ '^[0-9]+$' THEN route_id_text::bigint ELSE null END),
    migration_status = 'in_progress'
WHERE tenant_id = :TENTANT
  AND route_id_int IS NULL
  AND created_at < now() - interval '7 days'
LIMIT 100000;
```

mari-plat: We'll run that in a loop with sleep and IO budget.

anil: Add logging of rows processed + errors. Make sure we track unparsable text values; we might need a mapping table for legacy aliases.

sophia: Dashboard changes: Console UI needs to be tolerant — if route_id_int is null show fallback with a subtle badge "legacy id". Product will love that.

gabe: Alerting: create an alert if >1% of queries fallback to text after migration window.

jess: QA: run a small synthetic canary tenant that mimics heavy billing usage. We'll run the full pipeline and verify numbers match.

sre-oncall: We need a runbook entry — include rollback steps (stop dual-write; set query adapter to prefer text; revert indexes). Also schedule during low-traffic: Fri 02:00 UTC preferred.

mari-plat: I'll draft the runbook. Who can own the backfill orchestration? This needs someone to watch the loop and escalate.

anil: I can own orchestration for the first tenant cohort.

sophia: I'll own dashboard changes and console read adapter PRs.

gabe: I'll update billing batch jobs to read parity-mode.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: billing-ingest-v3 on host pool canary-3 at 2026-03-23T02:00:00Z :white_check_mark:

jess: One more thing — telemetry. We must add metrics to measure: `backfill_rows/sec`, `fallback_rate_pct`, `avg_query_ms_by_column`. Put dashboards in observability before starting.

mari-plat: Good call. I'll add those to the rollout checklist.

sophia: Risk we missed: historical denormalized snapshots used for exports (S3 nightly dumps) — they may need rework. Gabe can coordinate.

gabe: Yep I'll update export pipeline to use the read adapter.

anil: After we verify 30 days of stable usage, we plan index creation on `route_id_int` with `CONCURRENTLY` and then drop old text index and column.

sophia: Document change in console docs and API changelog too.

jess: Let's lock in times: propose starting schema add on 2026-03-23 02:00 UTC. Backfill will be ongoing; we'll grow cohorts over 2 weeks.

mari-plat: Ack. I'll open PRs for schema + dual-write and a temp feature flag. Thanks all — I'll post the runbook link once drafted. :sparkles:
